Members of Jawaharlal Nehru University Students' Union (JNUSU) ended their 17-day hunger strike on Tuesday. The development came after meetings between student representative and a committee headed by the university's dean.
A letter signed by Dean of school of social sciences, Vivek Kumar, said that the revocation of the rustication of five students has been directed. The students named in the letter are - Aditi Mishra, K Gopika Babu, Sunil Yadav, Danish Ali and Nitish Kumar.
The revocation of rustication of the JNUSU office bearers, including the president, was among the key demands of the students.
Here are 5 key things discussed in the meeting between students and the university committee:
Apart from this, discussions on hostel reservations and their structuring, library timings and opening of a canteen in CSLG were also held.
JNUSU members were demanding the reinstatement of rusticated office bearers. According to news agency PTI, the student union argued that it is an elected representative body with a mandate from around 9,000 students, and not merely a students' group. Its representatives have been elected through independent election committees and notified by the office of the dean of students, it said.
The union reportedly also alleged corruption in university recruitment and questioned the administration's commitment to protecting taxpayers' money.
On Monday, Vice-Chancellor (V-C) Santishree Dhulipudi Pandit said that a competent authority was willing to meet protesting students at 8.50 am on October 16 but no one was present on the site.
However, the students countered the claim, questioning the V-C's visit to the protest site at 9 am, saying it was aimed at creating a narrative that only a few students were participating in the agitation.
While JNUSU claimed that its rusticated office-bearers were denied medical check-ups during the hunger strike, the V-C said the administration has been "most democratic and humanitarian", and has not taken any action against the rusticated students, despite destruction of "public property worth ₹ 20 lakh".
